children: Brazil's rapid ethanol expansion is providing corn growers with an alternative to export channels for surplus production, increasing competition for available corn and supporting local prices, Rabobank senior economic analyst Marcela Marini says in a note. Ethanol producers need continuous year-round flow of feedstock and have significant on-site storage capacity, which provides a stable outlet for corn production. "The result is not an end to Brazil's exportable surplus, but a reduction in the volume that must be cleared through exports." Export parity is still an important price reference, but is becoming less dominant, Marini says. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
